name: Lantern Grove - continuous world
units: studs (1 stud = 0.3 m), +Y up, map view +X east/right, -Z north/up. Same axes as holes.json.

bounds.note: Terrain extent. Backdrop meshes sit outside it.

placement_convention.apply: For every holes.json element of hole N: rotate its LOCAL x/z about +Y by placement.yaw_deg, then translate by placement.origin. x' = lx*cos(yaw) + lz*sin(yaw) + origin.x ; z' = -lx*sin(yaw) + lz*cos(yaw) + origin.z ; y' = ly + origin.y. Piece yaw_world = piece.yaw + yaw_deg. Positive yaw = counter-clockwise in the map view (e.g. yaw 90 turns local -Z (play direction) to world -X/west; yaw 180 to world +Z/south).
placement_convention.roblox: holeRoot = CFrame.new(origin) * CFrame.Angles(0, math.rad(yaw_deg), 0); partCFrame = holeRoot * localCFrame. Moving-part pivots/axes and teleport points transform the same way (axes: rotate only).
placement_convention.supersedes: holes.json world_offset/world_yaw (the old flat layout) - ignore those, use world.json placements.

terrain.method: Deterministic heightfield h(x,z), evaluated in this order (see tools/worldlib.py height_at): (1) base: h = base.height + sum(amp*sin(2*pi*x/wx+px)*sin(2*pi*z/wz+pz)). (2) regions in list order. op 'set': w = 1-smoothstep(d/falloff) with d = distance outside the shape (0 inside); h += (height-h)*w. op 'hill': h += peak*cos^2(pi/2*q) for q = elliptical radius/radii < 1. (3) rim (then detail_noise, same formula as noise): q = superellipse radius ((|x-cx|/hx)^p+(|z-cz|/hz)^p)^(1/p); h += height*(1+variation*sin(lobes*atan2(z-cz,x-cx)+phase))*smoothstep((q-start)/(full-start)). (4) pads (one per hole, rules in terrain.pads). (5) paths: within width/2+1 of a path centreline (non on_hole/bridge segments) h = path profile (stairs: profile - stair_bed_drop), blended to the previous h over `shoulder` studs. (5b) felt clamp: under every non-bridge felt piece h = min(h, felt surface - felt_thickness). (6) water: h = min(h, stream/lake carve profile; lake: level+beach_slope*d within beach_width of the shore, then +bank_slope per stud). smoothstep(t)=t^2(3-2t) on t clamped to [0,1].

base.note: noise = before regions; detail_noise = added after regions+rim (before pads/paths/water), same formula

regions.material: rock face on the edge, grass/leafy on top
grass; rocky lip at Twin Falls

regions.note: Rocky knob at the village's NW corner; Lookout Rock viewing deck sits on the path beside it

rim.note: Forested rim hills hide the terrain edge

pads.rule: For each hole: felt pieces (non-overlay) transformed by its placement. Under any non-bridge felt piece the terrain = min over covering pieces of (felt surface - felt_thickness). Elsewhere inside footprint (felt+walls) + margin: h = max(lowest floor, max_i(floor_i - cone_slope*dist_to_piece_i)), blended to the previous terrain over `falloff` studs beyond the margin. Water/pit hazard rectangles are cut to (hazard surface - hazard_depth).

stream.name: Lantern Brook
stream.note: Polyline north->south. level = water surface (studs), width = water width. Between vertices level/width are linear; terrain is carved to the channel profile (bed = level-depth, banks rise bank_slope per stud beyond the water edge). Fill Water from bed to `level` along the polyline.

heightmap.mapping: pixel (i=col, j=row) centre -> x = bounds.x[0] + (i+0.5)*stud_per_px, z = bounds.z[0] + (j+0.5)*stud_per_px (row 0 = north edge, col 0 = west edge); y = y_min + gray/65535*(y_max-y_min) (16-bit) or gray/255 (8-bit preview)

legend.rule: terrain below a water surface (stream, mere, hazards): paint bed Mud, fill Water to level
dry ground within 3 studs of the stream / 10 of the mere and < 1.5 above water

materials.note: RGB values are Roblox's default terrain material colours (the colormap convention of the Terrain Editor import). materials-legend.png shows the legend.
